data.title: Hradiská – Svedkovia dávnych čias 2: the second volume on hillforts
data.excerpt: In the course of October we are publishing the second volume of our edited collection on hillforts and their inhabitants. The first volume appeared in 2015 and found a surprisingly large readership among specialists and the general public alike.
data.metaTitle: Hradiská – Svedkovia dávnych čias 2: a new volume

children.text: Our efforts of several months will soon be rewarded. In the course of October we will publish the 2nd volume of the edited collection on hillforts.

​ 
 The first edited volume on hillforts was published by our civic association Hradiská in 2015. We were rather taken aback by its success, since books of specialist papers in the field of archaeology are not, after all, among publishing bestsellers. Even so, the book reached a great many readers, both among specialists and among the general public. After the volume appeared, our publishing activity continued, above all in cooperation with Mr Igor Furugláš and his company Dwarf Digital Archeology. Together we published the magazine Digitálne hradiská (Digital Hillforts), the publication Oživená archeológia (Archaeology Brought to Life) and, in 2019, the book Skryté poklady (Hidden Treasures). We also worked with him on the creation of several unique 3D models of hillforts and of other vanished archaeological features, which thousands of people have seen. In addition, our association and its members, whose numbers have grown, have taken part as volunteers in a number of archaeological excavations in the territory of Slovakia and have established fruitful cooperation with many archaeologists. Archaeology attracts us greatly, and through our work we try to show that help from non-specialists during excavations is very valuable and important, and that metal detecting, for instance, can also be of considerable help and need not be destructive if it is carried out under the expert supervision of scholars.
 
 The present second volume of the collection on hillforts and their inhabitants is a natural continuation of our cooperation with archaeologists; in it you will find a great deal of hitherto unpublished information from renowned archaeologists, and even an upland site which members of our association discovered and later investigated together with archaeologists.
 
 The aim of the project is above all to support the scholarly work of Slovak archaeologists by enabling them to publish the results of their research on the subject of hillforts in print. A further aim is to popularise the results of archaeological research into hillforts in Slovakia and to bring the subject of hillforts closer to the non-specialist public as well. The volume will help to broaden readers' knowledge of the life of our ancestors. The contributions to the volume are provided by archaeologists who specialise in the study of the Early Middle Ages and prehistory in Slovakia and Ukraine. The volume will thus be a welcome addition to the modest amount of specialist archaeological literature published in Slovakia. The volume will run to about 240 pages in B5 format and, besides the text, will also contain a large number of illustrations.
